questions.question: Which statement about RAM is correct?
options: A. RAM keeps user files after the power is switched off.
B. RAM is application software used to edit photos.
C. RAM is volatile main memory that holds programs and data while they are in use.
D. RAM is the same thing as a solid-state drive.
questions.explanation: RAM is main memory and it is volatile, so its contents are lost when the power goes off. Files that must survive a shutdown belong in secondary storage.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Inside the CPU, which part performs calculations and logical comparisons?
options: A. The control unit.
B. The arithmetic and logic unit (ALU).
C. The printer.
D. The router.
questions.explanation: The ALU carries out arithmetic and comparisons. The control unit directs how instructions are carried out; it is not the part that adds the numbers.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: In a school hall, a projector shows the slides to the audience. In the input-process-output cycle the projector is used for:
options: A. Input.
B. Secondary storage.
C. Processing only.
D. Output.
questions.explanation: A projector presents results to people, so it is an output device. A keyboard, scanner or sensor would be input.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Which of the following is system software?
options: A. The operating system.
B. A web browser used to read the news.
C. A spreadsheet used for a club budget.
D. A photo editor.
questions.explanation: The operating system manages hardware, files and memory so that applications can run. A browser, a spreadsheet and a photo editor are application software.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Which program is a utility?
options: A. A word processor.
B. An online encyclopedia.
C. A slide-presentation application.
D. A backup utility.
questions.explanation: A backup utility is system software that does a housekeeping job. Word processors, encyclopedias and slide software are applications.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A touchscreen on a tablet is best described as:
options: A. An output device only.
B. Secondary storage.
C. Both an output device and an input device.
D. A type of ROM.
questions.explanation: The screen shows output, and touch is input. Calling it output only misses half of what it does.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A student saves a video project to an SSD and then shuts the computer down. The file is still there the next day because an SSD is:
options: A. Non-volatile secondary storage.
B. Volatile RAM.
C. The arithmetic and logic unit.
D. Application software.
questions.explanation: Secondary storage keeps files when the power is off. RAM would not. The ALU is part of the processor, not a place to store the video.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A program adds two test scores. Which component carries out that addition?
options: A. The control unit, because it stores files.
B. The ALU.
C. A barcode scanner.
D. The modem.
questions.explanation: Addition is arithmetic, so the ALU does it. A scanner and a modem are not processors, and the control unit does not replace the ALU.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Which device is used to capture a paper drawing so it can be stored as an image file?
options: A. A speaker.
B. A printer.
C. A scanner.
D. A projector.
questions.explanation: A scanner is an input device that captures an image from paper. Speakers, printers and projectors are output devices.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: In a computer system, the bus is:
options: A. The pathway that carries data and signals between components such as the CPU and memory.
B. A wide area network that joins two cities.
C. A kind of malware.
D. The primary key of a table.
questions.explanation: Here the bus is inside the computer, not a network topology and not a database key. It connects components so data and control signals can move.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A device driver is:
options: A. Application software for editing films.
B. System software that lets the operating system communicate with a particular device.
C. A hexadecimal colour code.
D. A foreign key.
questions.explanation: A driver is the system-software link between the operating system and a device such as a printer. It is not an application for making a film.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Why is RAM a poor place to keep the only copy of an attendance record?
options: A. RAM cannot store numbers.
B. RAM is a printer.
C. RAM is always larger than a hard disk.
D. RAM is volatile, so the record disappears when the power goes off.
questions.explanation: Volatility is the point. The record needs secondary storage if it must still be there after shutdown.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: The binary number 1101 is equal to which denary number?
questions.explanation: 1101 binary is 8 + 4 + 0 + 1 = 13. 14 would be 1110, and 11 would be 1011.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: In hexadecimal, the digit F has the denary value:
questions.explanation: Hexadecimal A to F means 10 to 15. F is 15, not a denary digit and not 10 (that is A).
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Two hexadecimal digits represent:
options: A. One byte.
B. Two bytes.
C. One bit.
D. One kilobyte.
questions.explanation: One hex digit is 4 bits. Two hex digits are 8 bits, which is one byte.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Why is Unicode used instead of ASCII when a document contains Chinese characters?
options: A. ASCII is an image format and Unicode is a sound format.
B. ASCII already contains every Chinese character, so Unicode is only for numbers.
C. Unicode can represent many writing systems, including Chinese, while ASCII cannot.
D. Unicode is a network cable.
questions.explanation: ASCII covers a small set of characters, mainly English letters and symbols. Unicode is the coding system that can represent Chinese and many other scripts.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: An image uses a colour depth of 8 bits per pixel. How many different colours can each pixel represent?
questions.explanation: The number of colours is 2 to the power of the colour depth. 2^8 = 256, not 8.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: An uncompressed bitmap is 100 pixels by 80 pixels with a colour depth of 4 bits. Its size is:
options: A. 4000 bytes.
B. 32000 bytes.
C. 800 bytes.
D. 4000 bits.
questions.explanation: Pixels = 100 × 80 = 8000. Bits = 8000 × 4 = 32000. Bytes = 32000 / 8 = 4000. The figure 32000 is the bit count, not the byte count.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A school logo must be enlarged on a banner without looking blocky. Which statement is correct?
options: A. A bitmap stays perfectly sharp at any size.
B. A vector graphic becomes pixelated when it is enlarged.
C. A bitmap may look blocky when enlarged; a vector graphic stays sharp.
D. Neither bitmaps nor vector graphics can be printed.
questions.explanation: A bitmap is a grid of pixels, so enlargement shows the blocks. A vector graphic stores shapes, so it scales cleanly.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A sound clip is recorded again at a higher sampling rate, with the same sample size, channels and duration, and it is not compressed. The uncompressed file:
options: A. Becomes smaller.
B. Becomes larger.
C. Turns into a vector graphic.
D. Loses its sample size.
questions.explanation: A higher sampling rate stores more samples per second, so the uncompressed file is larger, not smaller.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: An uncompressed mono clip lasts 5 seconds, sampled at 8000 Hz with an 8-bit sample size. The file size is:
options: A. 40000 bytes.
B. 320000 bytes.
C. 8000 bytes.
D. 5 bytes.
questions.explanation: Bytes = 8000 × 8 × 1 × 5 / 8 = 40000. Forgetting to divide by 8 produces 320000, which is the number of bits.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: The same uncompressed recording is stored once in mono and once in stereo, with every other setting unchanged. The stereo file is:
options: A. About half the size of the mono file.
B. The same size, because channels do not affect size.
C. A text file.
D. About twice the size of the mono file.
questions.explanation: Stereo has two channels, so the uncompressed size is about double the mono size.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: In the calculations in this course, 1 KB is taken as:
options: A. 1000 bits.
B. 1024 bytes.
C. 8 bytes.
D. 1024 bits.
questions.explanation: Unless a question states another convention, use 1 KB = 1024 bytes and 1 byte = 8 bits. 1024 bits would be only 128 bytes.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: The hexadecimal value 2F is equal to which denary number?
questions.explanation: 2 × 16 + 15 = 47. F is 15, not a denary digit, so 215 is a misreading of the symbols.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Thirty computers in one ICT room share a printer. This network is a:
options: A. WAN, because the computers can open websites.
B. CPU.
C. Database table.
D. LAN.
questions.explanation: A single room is a local area network. Being able to reach the Internet does not turn the room itself into a WAN.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: The job of a switch in a school LAN is to:
options: A. Connect devices and forward data to the device that needs it.
B. Translate domain names into IP addresses.
C. Encrypt every file stored on a hard disk.
D. Act as an input sensor.
questions.explanation: A switch works inside the LAN and forwards traffic to the intended device. DNS translates names, and encryption is a different control.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Which device forwards data between different networks?
options: A. A hub, because it always sends data to one chosen computer only.
B. A scanner.
C. A router.
D. A speaker.
questions.explanation: A router joins networks and forwards data using IP addresses. A hub repeats traffic inside a LAN; it does not route between networks.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: In a star topology, one cable between a computer and the central switch is unplugged. The usual result is:
options: A. Every computer in the school loses its connection.
B. Only the computer on that cable is disconnected.
C. The primary key of every database changes.
D. All files are converted to hexadecimal.
questions.explanation: Each device has its own link to the centre, so one cable fault affects that device. Failure of the central switch would be the wider outage.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: In a star LAN, the central switch fails. What happens?
options: A. Devices that depend on that switch can no longer use the LAN.
B. Nothing, because a star has no single point of failure.
C. The LAN becomes a personal database.
D. Only the colour depth of images changes.
questions.explanation: The central switch is a single point of failure in a star. Saying a star has no single point of failure is a common wrong answer.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Why might a school use fibre-optic cable between two buildings?
options: A. Fibre is always the cheapest cable, and that is its only advantage.
B. Fibre stores volatile RAM.
C. Fibre is application software.
D. It offers high bandwidth and is less affected by electrical interference.
questions.explanation: Fibre carries data as light. The syllabus advantages are bandwidth and resistance to electrical interference, not a claim that it is always the cheapest option.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A school file server holds pupils' work and each classroom computer logs on to use it. This arrangement is:
options: A. Peer-to-peer, because a server is involved.
B. Client-server.
C. A colour-depth setting.
D. A hexadecimal code.
questions.explanation: A dedicated server providing files to client computers is the client-server model. Peer-to-peer has no dedicated server.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Which description matches a peer-to-peer network?
options: A. One dedicated server provides accounts and files to every client.
B. It is a kind of malware.
C. Computers share directly, with no dedicated server.
D. It is a method of sampling sound.
questions.explanation: Peer-to-peer sharing has no dedicated server. That makes a small home setup simpler and a school backup plan weaker.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A modem is used to:
options: A. Enter a record into a database form.
B. Perform a dry run of pseudocode.
C. Store a primary key.
D. Connect the local network to the line from the Internet service provider.
questions.explanation: A modem links the home or school network to the ISP connection by converting signals for that line. It is not a database object.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: How does a hub differ from a switch?
options: A. A hub forwards data only to the destination device, while a switch sends it to every port.
B. A hub sends data to all of its ports, while a switch forwards it to the intended device.
C. A hub is an output device and a switch is a font.
D. A hub encrypts email and a switch does not.
questions.explanation: A hub repeats traffic to every port. A switch sends it to the device that should receive it, which wastes less of the LAN.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: An IP address is used to:
options: A. Identify a device on a network.
B. Replace a person's legal name on an identity card.
C. Prove that a song is free of copyright.
D. Validate that a mark is between 0 and 100.
questions.explanation: An IP address identifies a device so traffic can be delivered. It is not a copyright licence or a validation rule.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Wi-Fi in this course means:
options: A. A fibre-optic cable inside a wall.
B. A database relationship.
C. A wireless way for devices to join a LAN.
D. A lossless image format.
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi is wireless networking. It still needs security, such as a password, because the signal is not confined to a cable.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Which statement is correct?
options: A. The World Wide Web is a service that runs on the Internet.
B. The Internet and the World Wide Web are two names for the same thing.
C. The World Wide Web is a CPU.
D. The Internet can only carry email.
questions.explanation: The Internet is the global network. The Web is one service on it, using linked pages and HTTP or HTTPS. Email is another service, not the definition of the Internet.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: In the URL https://www.example.edu.hk/ict/notes.html, which part is the protocol?
options: A. www.example.edu.hk
B. /ict/notes.html
C. https
D. notes.html
questions.explanation: https is the protocol. The host name is www.example.edu.hk and the path is /ict/notes.html.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: DNS is used to:
options: A. Encrypt every file on a hard disk.
B. Translate a domain name into an IP address.
C. Choose a primary key.
D. Repeat a FOR loop.
questions.explanation: People type a domain name. DNS finds the IP address so the request can be delivered. It is not encryption and not a database key.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A student types a full URL into a program and a page appears. The student did not type any search words. The program is acting as:
options: A. A switch.
B. A firewall only.
C. A primary key.
D. A browser, not a search engine.
questions.explanation: A browser displays a page from a URL. A search engine is what you use when you search for pages. Opening one known address does not make the browser a search engine.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: HTTPS means that:
options: A. The words on the page must be true.
B. The site is owned by the government.
C. Data between the browser and the site is encrypted in transit.
D. No password is ever required.
questions.explanation: HTTPS encrypts the connection. It does not prove the page is accurate or that the owner is honest.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Which statement about email is correct?
options: A. Email uses the Internet, but it is not the same thing as the World Wide Web.
B. Email can only be stored as a bitmap.
C. Email is a kind of RAM.
D. Email is a star topology.
questions.explanation: Email is an Internet service. The Web is a different service, made of linked pages. Sending mail does not require the message to be a web page.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Downloading a file means:
options: A. Sending the file from your computer to a server.
B. Choosing a primary key.
C. Tracing a loop on paper.
D. Copying the file from a server to your device.
questions.explanation: Download is server to you. Upload is the opposite direction. A trace and a primary key are different topics.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A class keeps its report in cloud storage. The file will not open on a phone that has no signal because:
options: A. Cloud storage never uses a network.
B. The file is on a remote server that the phone cannot reach without a connection.
C. Cloud storage is a Trojan horse.
D. The file has become a hexadecimal digit.
questions.explanation: Cloud storage is remote. No connection means you cannot reach that copy. It is not malware by definition.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A student uploads homework to a folder shared only with the teacher. This means:
options: A. The file is not automatically published to the whole Web.
B. Every person on the Internet can edit it.
C. The school LAN is deleted.
D. A range check has failed.
questions.explanation: Uploading to a private share is not the same as making a public web page. The permission setting decides who can open it.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A local HTML page shows the heading correctly, but the photo is a broken icon. The most likely cause is:
options: A. The Internet service provider has cancelled the Web.
B. RAM is volatile.
C. The image file name or path written in the page is wrong.
D. The ALU cannot add numbers.
questions.explanation: The image is a separate file. A wrong name or folder in the page breaks the picture even when the text is fine, and a local page does not need the ISP for that test.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A hyperlink is:
options: A. The system bus inside a CPU.
B. A foreign key.
C. A sampling rate.
D. A link that points to another URL.
questions.explanation: A hyperlink is how a web page sends the reader to another address. It is not a database key or a hardware bus.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: At the level of this course, HTML is:
options: A. A set of steps for spreading a worm.
B. Markup that describes the structure of a page, such as headings and links.
C. An operating system.
D. A lossy audio format.
questions.explanation: HTML marks structure so a browser can display the page. It is not an operating system and not a method for attacking a network.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: In a table, a record and a field are:
options: A. A record is a column and a field is a row.
B. A record is one row and a field is one column.
C. Both words mean primary key.
D. A field is a network switch.
questions.explanation: One record is one row, such as one student. One field is one column, such as the class.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A primary key must:
options: A. Uniquely identify each record and must not be left empty.
B. Be allowed to repeat whenever two people share a name.
C. Always be a person's name.
D. Be a kind of malware.
questions.explanation: Uniqueness and no empty value are the rules. A name fails when two students share it, so a school-issued number is safer.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A foreign key is:
options: A. A second copy of a photograph stored as a bitmap.
B. An output device.
C. A sampling rate.
D. A field that stores the primary key of a related record in another table.
questions.explanation: The foreign key is how tables are linked. In a loan table, BorrowerID pointing at the borrower table is a foreign key.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: One borrower can have many loans, and each loan belongs to one borrower. How should this be stored?
options: A. As a one-to-one link that allows only one loan forever.
B. With the borrower's full address typed again on every loan, and no keys.
C. As a one-to-many relationship, storing the borrower id on each loan.
D. It cannot be stored in a database.
questions.explanation: One borrower to many loans is one-to-many. The borrower id on the loan record is the foreign key. Repeating the address on every loan creates conflicting copies.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Why is a student name a weak primary key?
options: A. Two students can have the same name, so the key would not be unique.
B. A name cannot be displayed on a form.
C. Names are always numbers.
D. A name is a WAN.
questions.explanation: A primary key must be unique. Shared names break that rule. A student number issued once does not.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Which statement is correct?
options: A. A form is a printed list of overdue books.
B. A form is used to enter or edit data; a report is formatted output.
C. A report is a firewall.
D. A form is a CPU.
questions.explanation: Use a form for input on screen and a report for a formatted list, often printed. Swapping the two words is a standard exam trap.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: In a query, a criterion is:
options: A. The order in which the matching records are sorted.
B. The colour of the form.
C. The condition a record must meet, such as Class = 4A.
D. The speed of the system bus.
questions.explanation: The criterion filters records. Sort order arranges the ones that remain; it does not replace the filter.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A mark field accepts only values from 0 to 100. The true mark is 60, but the clerk types 70. What happens?
options: A. The range check proves that 70 is the true mark.
B. The range check rejects 70.
C. The database reports a syntax error.
D. 70 is inside the range, so the range check does not catch the mistake.
questions.explanation: Validation tests whether the value is reasonable, not whether it is true. 70 is allowed. Only a check against the original script would catch the swap.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Asking a clerk to type each mark twice is an example of:
options: A. A colour-depth calculation.
B. Verification.
C. A worm.
D. A star topology.
questions.explanation: Double entry checks that the value was copied consistently. That is verification. It is not a range check, and it still fails if the same wrong number is typed twice.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Referential integrity means:
options: A. A firewall blocks every email.
B. A bitmap is stored in bytes.
C. A command word asks for a reason.
D. A foreign key must match an existing primary key.
questions.explanation: You should not be able to store a loan for a borrower id that is not in the borrower table. That rule is referential integrity.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A birthday should be stored in a field of type:
options: A. Date.
B. Yes/no, because a birthday is a choice.
C. Bitmap.
D. Untyped text, so that 31/02/2020 can be kept on purpose.
questions.explanation: A date field can reject impossible dates and can be sorted in calendar order. A yes/no field cannot hold a full date, and free text makes bad dates easy to store.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Which statement correctly separates validation and verification?
options: A. They are two names for the same check.
B. Verification tests a range; validation tests double entry.
C. Validation tests whether data is reasonable; verification tests whether it was copied accurately.
D. Neither check can be used on a form.
questions.explanation: Range, type and presence checks are validation. Double entry and proofreading are verification. A value can pass both and still be the wrong fact if it was copied consistently from a wrong source.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: JPEG is:
options: A. A lossless format and the usual choice for a logo with a transparent background.
B. A sound sampling rate.
C. A lossy image format commonly used for photographs.
D. A database key.
questions.explanation: JPEG throws away some detail to make photograph files smaller. It is a poor match for sharp text or a transparent logo.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Which description of PNG is correct?
options: A. PNG compression is lossy.
B. PNG can store only one colour.
C. PNG is a network topology.
D. PNG is lossless and can support transparency.
questions.explanation: PNG keeps the original image data and can include a transparent background, which is why it suits logos and screenshots.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A limitation of GIF is that:
options: A. It can store uncompressed 24-bit photographs with no colour limit.
B. It is limited to 256 colours.
C. It is a central processing unit.
D. It is the protocol that sends email.
questions.explanation: GIF uses at most 256 colours. That is acceptable for a simple icon or a short animation, and weak for a photograph.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: For a 30-second welcome message on a web page, why might the club choose MP3 rather than WAV?
options: A. MP3 is lossy compressed audio and is usually much smaller than an uncompressed WAV of the same clip.
B. WAV is always the smaller file.
C. MP3 is an image format.
D. MP3 is a primary key.
questions.explanation: MP3 discards some sound detail to save space. WAV is commonly uncompressed, so the same clip takes much more room. Use WAV when you need the larger master, not when the page must download quickly.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Lossy compression:
options: A. Can always restore every original bit.
B. Is a validation rule on a form.
C. Is a peer-to-peer network.
D. Reduces file size by discarding some of the original data.
questions.explanation: Lossy methods such as JPEG and MP3 throw detail away. Lossless compression is the one that can be reversed exactly.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Lossless compression:
options: A. Permanently deletes detail from a photograph.
B. Is a phishing message.
C. Can be reversed so the original data is restored.
D. Is a wide area network.
questions.explanation: Lossless compression packs data without throwing the original away. It is the safer choice for a logo or any file that must stay exact.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: An uncompressed bitmap is 640 by 480 pixels with 24-bit colour. Its size is:
options: A. 921600 bytes.
C. 307200 bytes.
D. 640 bytes.
questions.explanation: 640 × 480 × 24 / 8 = 921600 bytes. 307200 is the number of pixels. 921600 bits would forget that the 24 already counts bits and that the answer must still be divided by 8.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Both the width and the height of a bitmap are doubled. The number of pixels:
options: A. Doubles.
B. Becomes four times as large.
C. Stays the same.
D. Becomes an ASCII code.
questions.explanation: Doubling each side multiplies the area by four, so the uncompressed file size is about four times larger if the colour depth stays the same.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A vector logo is enlarged for a banner. The logo:
options: A. Must become blocky.
B. Becomes a worm.
C. Stays sharp because the shapes are stored as instructions.
D. Loses its copyright automatically.
questions.explanation: Vector graphics scale without pixelation. Enlarging them does not cancel copyright.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Captions on a school video are useful because they:
options: A. Let viewers follow the video without relying only on the soundtrack.
B. Increase the colour depth to 1 bit.
C. Act as a primary key.
D. Replace the need for a copyright licence.
questions.explanation: Captions support access, including for users who cannot hear the audio. They do not clear copyright or change the pixel format.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: The union crest must keep a transparent background on the website. Why is JPEG a poor choice?
options: A. JPEG is required by every browser for transparent logos.
B. JPEG is a sound format.
C. JPEG is a database report.
D. JPEG does not give a clean transparent background and can blur sharp edges.
questions.explanation: Use PNG or a vector file for a crest with transparency. JPEG is for photographs, where a little lost detail is acceptable.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: When starting a multimedia page, the club should first:
options: A. Pick the largest uncompressed files available.
B. Decide the audience and the purpose, then choose a format and size that fit.
C. Avoid text alternatives.
D. Auto-play sound so that every user must hear it.
questions.explanation: Audience and purpose drive the format. A huge uncompressed file, missing alternative text, or forced sound makes the page harder to use.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: In the pseudocode used in this course, the symbol ← means:
options: A. Compare two values and choose a branch.
B. Send an email.
C. Declare a primary key.
D. Assign a value to a variable.
questions.explanation: total ← 0 stores 0 in total. A comparison belongs in a condition such as IF mark >= 50. Do not treat the arrow as a test.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: What is the output of this pseudocode? sum ← 0; FOR i FROM 1 TO 3; sum ← sum + i; END FOR; OUTPUT sum
questions.explanation: sum becomes 1, then 3, then 6. The output is the sum, not the final value of i and not the starting 0.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: IF ... THEN ... ELSE ... ENDIF is an example of:
options: A. Iteration that always runs both branches.
B. Secondary storage.
C. Selection.
D. DNS.
questions.explanation: Selection chooses one branch. Only the THEN steps or the ELSE steps run, not both. Iteration is FOR or WHILE.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A pass should be given for a mark of 50 or above. The algorithm says IF mark > 50 THEN OUTPUT "Pass" ELSE OUTPUT "Fail" ENDIF, and mark is 50. What is true?
options: A. The output is Fail, because 50 does not satisfy mark > 50.
B. The output is Pass, because 50 is a pass in everyday language.
C. Both Pass and Fail are output.
D. The algorithm cannot run, because IF is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Trace the condition that is written. 50 is not greater than 50, so ELSE runs. The mismatch with "50 or above" is a logic error, not a syntax error.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: FOR i FROM 1 TO 4 means i takes the values:
options: C. 1 and 4 only
questions.explanation: The counter starts at 1 and stops after 4, so there are four passes: 1, 2, 3 and 4.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: What is the output of this pseudocode? n ← 1; WHILE n < 8; n ← n * 2; END WHILE; OUTPUT n
questions.explanation: n goes 1, 2, 4, 8. When n is 8 the condition n < 8 is false, so the loop stops and 8 is output. It does not multiply once more to 16.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A program runs and prints the wrong total because the loop adds one extra time. This is a:
options: A. Logic error.
B. Syntax error.
C. Fibre-optic fault.
D. Primary-key error.
questions.explanation: The program runs, so the language rules were followed, but the result is wrong. That is a logic error. A syntax error would stop it from running.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Which is a syntax error?
options: A. Using > when the specification says >=, while the rest of the program runs.
B. Dividing by zero while the program is running.
C. Leaving out ENDIF, so the program breaks the language rules and does not run.
D. Testing a mark of 50.
questions.explanation: A missing ENDIF breaks the structure, so the program is not run. A wrong comparison that still runs is a logic error. Dividing by zero during a run is a runtime error.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Valid marks are from 0 to 100 inclusive. Which pair is boundary test data?
options: A. 63 and 64
B. The letter A and a blank photo
C. A normal essay title
D. 0 and 100
questions.explanation: 0 and 100 sit on the edges of the allowed range. 63 is normal data. The letter A is abnormal data.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Which input is abnormal test data for a numeric mark?
options: A. The letter A.
B. The mark 63.
C. The mark 100.
D. The mark 0.
questions.explanation: A letter is the wrong type, so it is abnormal or erroneous. 63 is normal. 0 and 100 are boundaries.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A dry run is:
options: A. Installing a program from an unknown website.
B. Printing a database report.
C. Executing an algorithm on paper, usually with a trace table.
D. Encrypting a disk.
questions.explanation: A dry run walks through the steps and records variable values. It is how you check a loop before you trust the output.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: When a question asks for the output of a given algorithm, you should:
options: A. Add a division step if you think the result would be more useful.
B. Output only what the written steps produce.
C. Change every ← into a comparison.
D. Run both branches of an IF.
questions.explanation: Marks come from the steps on the page. Extra helpful steps are not part of the trace, and only one branch of an IF runs.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A virus is malware that:
options: A. Attaches to a host file and spreads when that file is shared and run.
B. Spreads across a network by itself without a host file.
C. Is a lawful backup method.
D. Is a primary key.
questions.explanation: A virus needs a host file. A worm is the malware that spreads across a network by itself. Do not use the word virus for every threat.
questions.subject: ict
questions.syllabus_ref: Compulsory: threats, security and safe use

questions.question: A worm is different from a virus because a worm:
options: A. Can only exist inside a document that a user chooses to open.
B. Is a lossless image format.
C. Is freeware.
D. Spreads across a network by itself.
questions.explanation: A worm does not need to attach to a host file. That is the contrast with a virus.
questions.subject: ict
questions.syllabus_ref: Compulsory: threats, security and safe use

questions.question: A Trojan horse:
options: A. Copies itself across a LAN without anyone installing it.
B. Is a star topology.
C. Appears to be useful software and does not replicate by itself.
D. Is a range check.
questions.explanation: A Trojan relies on someone installing a program that looks legitimate. It is not a worm and not a network layout.
questions.subject: ict
questions.syllabus_ref: Compulsory: threats, security and safe use

questions.question: A message that copies the school logo and asks you to type your portal password is:
options: A. A firewall rule.
B. Phishing.
C. A trace table.
D. A vector graphic.
questions.explanation: Phishing imitates a trusted sender to steal a password or personal data. The logo does not make the message genuine. Do not type the password.
questions.subject: ict
questions.syllabus_ref: Compulsory: threats, security and safe use

questions.question: Ransomware has encrypted files on one school computer. The appropriate response is to:
options: A. Pay at once from petty cash and tell nobody.
B. Send the administrator password to the address in the message.
C. Publish the files on the Web so the demand no longer matters.
D. Disconnect the computer, tell a teacher or technician, and restore from a clean backup.
questions.explanation: Payment is not a recovery plan, and the password must not be sent. Isolate the machine and recover from a backup that was not encrypted with it.
questions.subject: ict
questions.syllabus_ref: Compulsory: threats, security and safe use

questions.question: A firewall:
options: A. Encrypts every file on a disk as its main job.
B. Filters network traffic according to rules.
C. Proves that a website is honest.
D. Is a foreign key.
questions.explanation: A firewall allows or blocks connections. Encryption protects the contents of data. Neither one proves that a website tells the truth.
questions.subject: ict
questions.syllabus_ref: Compulsory: threats, security and safe use

questions.question: Which statement about HTTPS is correct?
options: A. It encrypts traffic in transit, but it does not prove the site owner is honest.
B. It guarantees that every sentence on the page is accurate.
C. It replaces the need for a backup.
D. It is a kind of primary key.
questions.explanation: HTTPS protects the connection from being read on the way. A lock icon is not a fact-check and not a backup.
questions.subject: ict
questions.syllabus_ref: Compulsory: threats, security and safe use

questions.question: Which practice is unsafe?
options: A. Using a long password that is not reused on other sites.
B. Adding a code from a phone as a second check.
C. Using the password "teacher" on several school and personal sites.
D. Keeping the password off a note stuck to the monitor.
questions.explanation: "teacher" is short, guessable and reused. Length, uniqueness and not sharing are the safe habits. A second factor adds something you have.
questions.subject: ict
questions.syllabus_ref: Compulsory: threats, security and safe use

questions.question: A useful backup of examination marks is:
options: A. The only copy, kept on the same disk as the original file.
B. A separate copy, stored somewhere else, and tested by restoring a file.
C. A copy left only in RAM.
D. A copy pasted into a phishing reply.
questions.explanation: A copy on the same disk dies with that disk. A backup has to be separate, and you only know it works if a restore has been tried.
questions.subject: ict
questions.syllabus_ref: Compulsory: threats, security and safe use

questions.question: Anti-malware software:
options: A. Removes the need for any backup.
B. Is a copyright licence.
C. Needs updates, because new malware appears after the last list was made.
D. Translates domain names into IP addresses.
questions.explanation: Detection lists go out of date. Updates help, and they still do not replace a backup or a careful user.
questions.subject: ict
questions.syllabus_ref: Compulsory: threats, security and safe use

questions.question: Pharming is a threat in which:
options: A. A loop is traced on paper.
B. An image is compressed without losing data.
C. A primary key is chosen.
D. A user is redirected to a fake site, often after name lookup has been interfered with.
questions.explanation: Pharming can send someone to a fake site even when they typed the real name. The exam point is the effect: do not trust the page, and do not enter a password. The steps used to interfere with name lookup are not required.
questions.subject: ict
questions.syllabus_ref: Compulsory: threats, security and safe use

questions.question: Before leaving a shared library computer, a student should:
options: A. Sign out of email so the next person cannot use the account.
B. Leave the session open to save logging in later.
C. Post the class sharing link on a public page.
D. Write the password on the monitor.
questions.explanation: An open session is unauthorised access waiting for the next user. Sign out, and do not leave the password in sight.
questions.subject: ict
questions.syllabus_ref: Compulsory: threats, security and safe use

questions.question: In Hong Kong, copyright in an original photograph or song:
options: A. Exists only after the owner pays a registration fee.
B. Applies only to software.
C. Arises automatically.
D. Applies only to database tables.
questions.explanation: Copyright protects original work without a registration step. A song, a photo, a video and program code can all be protected. School use is not a general exemption.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A student writes "I do not own this song" under a video that uses a commercial track. The caption:
options: A. May show the work is not the student's, but it is not copyright permission.
B. Makes the copying lawful for any audience.
C. Turns the song into freeware.
D. Is a firewall.
questions.explanation: A credit can address plagiarism. It does not replace a licence or the owner's consent. Freeware is a software arrangement and does not cover the song.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Freeware means the software:
options: A. Has no copyright and includes a duty to publish your changes.
B. Costs nothing to use, but it is still under copyright.
C. Gives you the right to copy any file on the Web.
D. Is a worm.
questions.explanation: Free of charge is not the same as open source, and it is not permission to copy unrelated music or logos. The freeware program itself remains copyrighted.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Open-source software:
options: A. Has no licence at all.
B. Is defined only as "it costs no money".
C. Is a sampling rate.
D. Allows the source code to be read and changed under the terms of its licence.
questions.explanation: The licence can still require credit or that you share changes. Open source is not "no rules", and it is not identical to freeware.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Shareware is software that:
options: A. Can be tried, and then paid for if you continue to use it.
B. Is a LAN cable.
C. Is a range check.
D. Has lost its copyright because it was placed on the Internet.
questions.explanation: The trial is the point of shareware. Keeping it after the trial without paying breaks the licence. Putting something on the Internet does not cancel copyright.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A lunch poll only needs a class and a menu choice. Which collection is excessive?
options: A. The class.
B. The menu choice.
C. The student's Hong Kong identity-card number.
D. Nothing, because more data is always better.
questions.explanation: Personal data should be limited to what the purpose needs. An identity-card number identifies the student far beyond a lunch choice, so it should not be collected "just in case".
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: The club emails a spreadsheet of every member's phone number to all members. This is a problem because:
options: A. A range check forbids spreadsheets.
B. Phone numbers cannot be personal data.
C. Email is the same thing as the World Wide Web.
D. People who do not need the numbers can now see them.
questions.explanation: The list should be available only to the people who have to make contact. Sending it to everyone fails the security and use principles. A phone number is personal data.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: The digital divide refers to:
options: A. A difference between two monitor sizes only.
B. Unequal access to devices, connectivity or skills.
C. A type of primary key.
D. A FOR loop.
questions.explanation: The gap can be equipment, a connection, or the skills to use them. It is also why accessible design, such as text alternatives, matters.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Ergonomics in a computer room means:
options: A. Choosing a malware scanner.
B. Writing a URL.
C. Setting up the chair, screen and breaks so that long use causes less physical strain.
D. Converting a number to hexadecimal.
questions.explanation: Eye strain, repetitive strain and backache are reduced by furniture, screen height and breaks. That is a health issue in the social-implications topic.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: After a signup is finished, the personal data collected for it should be:
options: A. Kept forever because storage is cheap.
B. Posted on a public story.
C. Left only in RAM and nowhere else, including no deletion decision.
D. Kept no longer than the purpose requires.
questions.explanation: Retention should match the purpose. When the signup is over, delete what you no longer need rather than building an unnecessary archive of phone numbers.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Text alternatives on images support equity of access because they:
options: A. Help users who cannot see the image.
B. Cancel the photographer's copyright.
C. Are a Trojan horse.
D. Double the sampling rate.
questions.explanation: A description lets more people use the page, including people using a screen reader. It does not license the image.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Which is a health reason to take breaks and adjust a workstation?
options: A. A syntax error in pseudocode.
B. Eye strain and repetitive strain from long computer use.
C. A foreign-key mismatch.
D. A star-topology cable fault.
questions.explanation: Physical strain is a health consequence of ICT use. The other options are technical faults, not health effects.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A question says "State two advantages" and is worth 2 marks. The answer should be:
options: A. A long paragraph about a related topic, with reasons and examples.
B. Two short points, one for each mark.
C. A complete program in a named language, even though none was requested.
D. A supply-and-demand diagram.
questions.explanation: "State" wants brief facts. Two marks means two points. An explanation belongs to "explain", and a diagram from another subject does not answer this stem.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: On the assessment framework used for recent HKDSE ICT years, Paper 1 is:
options: A. The paper on which you choose two electives.
B. School-based assessment only.
C. The compulsory paper, with a multiple-choice section and a short or structured section.
D. A practical test in another subject.
questions.explanation: Paper 1 covers the compulsory part and everyone answers it. Paper 2 is the elective paper. Confirm the framework for your exam year in case a later handbook changes a detail.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: On that same framework, Paper 2 requires candidates to:
options: A. Answer all three electives.
B. Answer multiple-choice questions only.
C. Ignore the electives and repeat Paper 1.
D. Answer all the questions in any two of Databases, Web Application Development, and Algorithm and Programming.
questions.explanation: You prepare the two electives your school enters, and you answer the questions on those two. You do not answer the third elective in the exam.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: The command word "suggest" means you should:
options: A. Give a practical idea that fits the case in the question.
B. Copy a definition and ignore the case.
C. Use the same sentence for every school described.
D. Draw a trace table even if the question is about a network.
questions.explanation: A suggestion has to work for the stem: a campus with two buildings is not answered by a generic word with no link to that campus.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: The command word "explain" means you should:
options: A. Name a term and stop, even when the mark allocation is more than one.
B. Leave units off a calculation.
C. Give a reason, not only the name of the idea.
D. Describe a worm by listing steps that would spread it.
questions.explanation: "Explain" needs the because. Naming the device without saying why it fits the case drops the marks. Do not answer a security question with instructions for an attack.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Which point would score as an advantage of a star over a bus?
options: A. Fibre is always cheaper than copper.
B. A fault in one link usually affects only one device.
C. A star has no single point of failure of any kind.
D. A star is a type of malware.
questions.explanation: One cable in a star serves one device, so that fault stays local. The central switch is still a single point of failure, so option C is too strong. Fibre is a medium, not a topology.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: State the output of this pseudocode: mark ← 50; IF mark > 50 THEN OUTPUT "Pass" ELSE OUTPUT "Fail" ENDIF.
options: A. Fail
B. Pass
D. The program cannot run.
questions.explanation: 50 is not greater than 50, so the ELSE branch runs and the output is Fail. Everyday ideas about a pass mark do not override the symbol in the algorithm.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A calculation question asks for the size of an uncompressed bitmap in bytes. A complete answer:
options: A. Gives the pixel count and no unit.
B. Reports the bit total and calls it bytes.
C. Omits the colour depth.
D. Shows width × height × colour depth / 8 and states the unit bytes.
questions.explanation: The division by 8 converts bits to bytes. Missing working or the wrong unit loses the mark even when part of the multiplication is right.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Which contrast is the one examiners expect?
options: A. The Internet and the World Wide Web are identical.
B. The World Wide Web is one service running on the Internet.
C. Email is a solid-state drive.
D. A browser and a search engine must be the same product.
questions.explanation: Keep Internet, Web, browser and search engine apart. Mixing them is one of the traps that returns every year.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Which statement should you keep in mind for a data-check question?
options: A. A range check does not prove that the typed value is the true value.
B. Validation and verification are the same process.
C. A primary key may safely contain duplicates.
D. RAM keeps files after the computer is switched off.
questions.explanation: Valid data can still be wrong. Say what the check catches and what it misses. The other three statements are standard false claims.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: School-based assessment in ICT, as described in the current handbook, includes:
options: A. A replacement for the compulsory paper.
B. Only a public multiple-choice paper.
C. A test from a different subject.
D. Guided tasks on design and implementation and on testing and evaluation.
questions.explanation: SBA is the two guided tasks, alongside the public papers, not instead of Paper 1. Check the handbook for your cohort for the exact mark split.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: The reliable way to answer an algorithm trace is to:
options: A. Add a step that would make the result look more sensible.
B. Write the output you expected before you read the conditions.
C. Follow the steps that are written and record each variable that changes.
D. Skip any value that sits on a boundary.
questions.explanation: The trace table is the answer. Boundaries are where wrong comparison symbols show up, so they are the values you should not skip.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Which statement about cache memory is correct?
options: A. Cache is the only place a user's files are kept after the computer is switched off.
B. Cache is application software used to edit video.
C. Cache is a small, fast store that keeps copies of data the CPU is likely to need again soon.
D. Cache replaces secondary storage, so a computer no longer needs a drive.
questions.explanation: Cache sits close to the CPU and speeds up repeated access. It is not a backup of files, and it does not replace an SSD or the operating system.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A computer can show its first start-up screen before the operating system has loaded from the SSD. Where are those start-up instructions typically kept?
options: A. In ROM, because the instructions must still be there after the power has been off.
B. Only in RAM, because RAM keeps its contents with no power.
C. In the projector, because output devices store programs.
D. In a spreadsheet the user has not created yet.
questions.explanation: ROM is non-volatile and holds the start-up instructions. RAM is volatile, and a display does not store the boot program.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A CPU has two cores. Which statement is the careful one?
options: A. Every program always runs exactly twice as fast.
B. Two cores mean the computer no longer needs RAM.
C. A core is a type of cable used only for printers.
D. Two cores can work on suitable tasks at the same time, but one single-threaded program does not automatically finish in half the time.
questions.explanation: Extra cores help when work can be split. A program that runs as one sequence still follows that sequence, so the speed-up is not automatic.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A pupil saves a project to a cloud drive. Which description fits this course?
options: A. The cloud replaces the CPU, so no processor is involved.
B. The file is held in secondary storage on a remote system and is reached over a network. A CPU still does the processing.
C. Cloud storage is volatile RAM inside the keyboard.
D. A cloud drive is a virus scanner and does not store files.
questions.explanation: Cloud storage is still storage, reached through a network. Processing stays with a computer's CPU. The file is not kept in RAM after a shutdown.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: The binary number 101101 is equal to which denary number?
questions.explanation: 101101 is 32 + 0 + 8 + 4 + 0 + 1 = 45. Place values from the left are 32, 16, 8, 4, 2 and 1.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: The hexadecimal number A3 is equal to which denary number?
questions.explanation: A is 10 in denary. A3 is 10 × 16 + 3 = 163. Two hex digits are not the same as the denary number 103.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: An 8-bit unsigned integer stores whole numbers from 0 to 255. Which sum cannot be stored in that format?
questions.explanation: 250 + 10 = 260, which is above 255, so it overflows an 8-bit unsigned integer. The other three sums are 250, 200 and 16, all inside the range.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: The word NOTE is stored as four ASCII characters, with no spaces. How many bytes does that text use in this course?
options: A. 4 bits for the whole word.
B. 4 bytes, because each ASCII character uses one byte.
C. 32 bytes, because each character uses 8 bytes.
D. 1 byte for the whole word.
questions.explanation: In the ASCII model used here, one character is one byte. Four characters are 4 bytes, which is 32 bits, not 32 bytes.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Which statement separates bandwidth from latency?
options: A. Bandwidth and latency are two names for the same measurement.
B. Bandwidth is the brand name of a switch.
C. Bandwidth is how much data can be moved in a given time. Latency is the delay before the data starts to arrive.
D. Latency is the number of computers joined to a star.
questions.explanation: A link can carry a lot of data and still feel slow if each response is delayed. Quote the quantity the question asks for.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: On a school Wi-Fi network, the SSID is:
options: A. The name of the wireless network, not the password itself.
B. The secret key that encrypts every file on the SSD.
C. A type of fibre-optic cable.
D. The operating system.
questions.explanation: The SSID is what you select in the list of networks. The password is a separate check. Knowing the name does not log you in.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A classroom computer has an address that begins 192.168. Which statement matches this course?
options: A. The address proves the computer has no network interface.
B. It is always the public address of a website on the World Wide Web.
C. It shows the file is stored in ROM.
D. That form is typically a private address used inside the LAN. A router is used when traffic must reach a different network.
questions.explanation: Addresses in the 192.168 range are private and used inside a local network. Crossing to another network is the router's job, not the switch's.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Why might a fixed computer in the ICT lab use a cable rather than Wi-Fi?
options: A. A cable can only connect a printer and cannot carry data.
B. A dedicated cable is less affected by walls and by other wireless users than a shared Wi-Fi channel.
C. Wi-Fi always has a higher bandwidth than any cable.
D. Using a cable turns that one computer into a WAN.
questions.explanation: A cabled link for a desk that does not move avoids sharing the wireless channel. One cable does not create a wide area network.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Which statement separates a browser from a search engine?
options: A. They are the same program with two names.
B. A search engine replaces DNS, so domain names are never used.
C. A browser displays pages. A search engine is a service, often opened in the browser, that returns links for keywords.
D. A browser can only send email and cannot show a page.
questions.explanation: You can type a full URL into a browser without using a search. A search engine finds pages. DNS still translates the domain name.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: At the level of this course, a cookie is:
options: A. A small piece of data a site can store so the browser can be recognised on a later visit, such as a language choice.
B. A hardware cache inside the CPU.
C. Another name for a computer virus.
D. The protocol shown by https.
questions.explanation: A cookie remembers a small fact between visits. It is not malware by itself, and it is not the HTTPS protocol.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Which statement about a URL and an IP address is correct?
options: A. A URL and an IP address are always the same text.
B. An IP address is a picture file format.
C. DNS deletes pages that have a URL.
D. A URL names a resource and often includes a domain. An IP address identifies a host. DNS links a domain name to an address.
questions.explanation: People use names. Networks use addresses. DNS is the lookup, not a delete tool, and a URL is not itself an image format.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Why is a large download described as travelling in packets?
options: A. The whole file must occupy one unbroken cable across the Internet until the download ends.
B. The data is split into packets that can be routed across the network and reassembled at the destination.
C. Packets are used only when a page is printed.
D. A packet is a primary key in a database.
questions.explanation: Packet switching lets pieces of one transfer share the network with other traffic. The receiving computer puts the pieces back in order.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A pupil table stores Class and ClassNo. Neither field is unique on its own, but each pair identifies one pupil. Which key fits?
options: A. Class alone, because a class name never repeats.
B. A photograph field, because pictures are always unique.
C. A composite primary key made from Class and ClassNo together.
D. No key is possible once any single field repeats.
questions.explanation: A composite key uses two or more fields that are unique as a group. Class by itself repeats, so it cannot be the primary key alone.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: House points are stored as text. A sort puts "100" before "20". Why can that happen?
options: A. Text is ordered character by character, so "100" can come before "20".
B. A text field cannot be shown on a form.
C. Every numeric field sorts 100 before 20 as well.
D. A primary key must be stored as text, so the order is required.
questions.explanation: The first character "1" comes before "2". Store quantities as numbers if you need numeric order.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A query uses Form = 5 AND House = "Red". Which rows are returned?
options: A. Every Form 5 row, plus every Red House row from other forms.
B. Only rows that fail both tests.
C. No rows, because AND deletes the two fields.
D. Only rows that are Form 5 and also Red House.
questions.explanation: AND keeps a row only when both criteria are true. OR would keep a row that matches either criterion. The fields stay in the table.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: The same home address is typed into every loan row for one borrower. Which problem does that create?
options: A. Repeating the address always makes the primary key unique.
B. An update can change one copy and miss the others, so the stored addresses disagree.
C. The repetition is required for referential integrity.
D. Repeating the address removes any chance of a typing error.
questions.explanation: Redundant copies drift apart when only one is edited. A borrower table held once, and linked by a key, avoids that.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Which statement separates MIDI from a WAV recording?
options: A. MIDI is always a larger recording of a speaking voice.
B. WAV stores only note instructions and no samples.
C. MIDI stores note, instrument and timing instructions. A WAV file stores sampled sound.
D. Both formats are lossy photograph standards.
questions.explanation: MIDI is compact because it stores instructions. Sampled audio stores the waveform, so a WAV of the same piece is usually much larger.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: An audio file is described as 128 kbps. In this course that figure means:
options: A. About 128 kilobits of audio data are used for each second of playback.
B. The picture is 128 pixels wide.
C. The sampling rate is 128 hertz and no data rate is involved.
D. The clip uses 128 speakers.
questions.explanation: Bit rate is data per second. It is not the width of an image and it is not the number of speakers.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A clip has 10 frames. Each frame is an uncompressed bitmap of 100 by 50 pixels with 8-bit colour. Ignoring sound, the video data size is:
options: A. 500 bytes.
B. 40 000 bytes.
C. 10 bytes.
D. 50 000 bytes.
questions.explanation: One frame is 100 × 50 × 8 = 40 000 bits = 5 000 bytes. Ten frames are 50 000 bytes. 40 000 is the bit count of one frame, not the byte count of the clip.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Why does a club draw a storyboard before filming sports day?
options: A. A storyboard compresses a JPEG file.
B. It plans the shots and their order, so a missing scene is spotted before the event is over.
C. It removes the need for any audio.
D. It is the primary key of the video database.
questions.explanation: A storyboard is a plan, not a compression method and not a database key. Filming from a plan avoids discovering a gap after the day has ended.

questions.question:
What is the output of this pseudocode?

a ← 3
b ← 4
a ← a + b
OUTPUT a
OUTPUT b
options: A. 3, then 4
B. 7, then 7
C. 7, then 4
D. 4, then 3
questions.explanation: a becomes 3 + 4 = 7. b is never assigned again, so it stays 4. The two OUTPUT lines print 7 and then 4.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question:
What is the output?

p ← 10
FOR k FROM 1 TO 3
    p ← p - 2
END FOR
OUTPUT p
questions.explanation: The body runs for k = 1, 2 and 3. p goes 10 → 8 → 6 → 4. Stopping after one pass gives 8. A fourth pass would give 2, but the loop stops at 3.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question:
What is the output?

score ← 40
bonus ← 0
IF score >= 50 THEN
    bonus ← 10
ELSE
    bonus ← 5
ENDIF
OUTPUT score + bonus
questions.explanation: 40 is not greater than or equal to 50, so the ELSE branch sets bonus to 5. The output is 40 + 5 = 45. The THEN branch does not run.

questions.question: How many times does the body of FOR i FROM 1 TO 5 run, and what is n after n ← 0 followed by n ← n + 1 inside that loop?
options: A. The body runs 4 times and n is 4.
B. The body runs 5 times and n is 5.
C. The body runs 6 times and n is 6.
D. The body runs once and n is 1.
questions.explanation: FROM 1 TO 5 includes both ends, so i is 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5. That is five additions, and n finishes at 5.

questions.question: Which statement separates authentication from authorisation?
options: A. They are two names for a firewall rule that blocks every website.
B. Authentication means deleting the only backup.
C. Authentication checks who the user is. Authorisation checks what that identity is allowed to do.
D. Authorisation means a file is stored with no access check at all.
questions.explanation: Logging in answers who you are. Permission to open a particular folder answers what you may do. A firewall is a different control.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A new wireless router still uses the password printed as "admin". What should the school do first?
options: A. Change it to a long password that only the school keeps, before the router is used.
B. Publish the printed password on the school website so every class can share it.
C. Leave it, because a password that came with the device cannot be guessed.
D. Email the printed password to every pupil.
questions.explanation: A default password is widely known for that model. Changing it is a basic safeguard. Sharing it removes the check.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Two-factor authentication, at the level of this course, means:
options: A. The same password is reused on two websites.
B. The firewall is switched off.
C. Passwords are stored in a folder that anyone on the Internet can open.
D. The user provides something they know and a second check, such as a code sent to a device they have.
questions.explanation: The second factor is a separate check, not a second copy of the same password and not a reason to disable other controls.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Which statement about HTTPS is accurate for this course?
options: A. Encryption means the site has no password and anyone may change it.
B. Encryption means someone who only intercepts the traffic cannot read the page contents without the proper key.
C. It proves that the downloaded file is a virus.
D. It replaces the need to keep any backup.
questions.explanation: HTTPS protects the contents in transit. It does not scan a file for malware, and it does not remove the need for a backup.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A pupil copies a chart from a news site, names the site, and posts the chart on the club's public page. Which statement is careful?
options: A. Attribution always replaces copyright.
B. A news chart may always be republished once the site name is written underneath.
C. Naming the source is honest attribution, but it is not the same as having permission to copy the chart.
D. Naming the source makes the chart the pupil's own work.
questions.explanation: Credit and permission are different. Unless a licence or the owner allows the use, copying it onto a public page can still infringe copyright.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A lunch poll asks for an HKID number, a home address and a parent's salary. What is the careful objection?
options: A. Those items are more than the poll needs. The club should collect only the choice it will use.
B. Collecting more personal data always makes a poll fairer.
C. A salary is required on every school form.
D. Collecting less personal data is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Data minimisation means you collect what the task needs and no more. A lunch choice does not need an identity number or a salary.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: An assembly video has no captions and no transcript. Who is left out?
options: A. Only pupils who dislike the speaker.
B. Nobody, because a video is accessible by default.
C. Only the person who operated the camera.
D. Pupils who cannot follow the soundtrack, including some who are deaf or hard of hearing.
questions.explanation: Captions and a transcript give another way to follow the words. A soundtrack alone does not serve every pupil.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: Which arrangement reduces strain in a long ICT lesson?
options: A. A screen on the floor so the neck stays bent for the whole lesson.
B. A screen near eye level, a supported back, and short breaks to look away and move.
C. No breaks, because rests are what cause strain.
D. The dimmest possible screen in a dark room, with no other change.
questions.explanation: Ergonomics covers posture, screen position and breaks. Working without a pause, or bending the neck for an hour, increases strain.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: In this course, the command word "compare" means you should:
options: A. Give only the advantages of the first item and ignore the second.
B. Copy a definition of one term and stop.
C. Point out similarities and differences, using both of the things named in the question.
D. State a number and leave the unit out.
questions.explanation: A comparison needs both sides. A one-sided list of advantages does not show how the two items differ or match.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A pupil works out 200 × 100 × 24 and writes 480 000. The question asked for the size in bytes. What is still missing?
options: A. Divide by 8, because 480 000 is a number of bits, and state the unit bytes.
B. Multiply by 8 again.
C. Nothing, because 480 000 is already in megabytes.
D. Remove the colour depth, because it is not part of a bitmap size.
questions.explanation: Width × height × colour depth gives bits. There are 8 bits in a byte, so the size is 480 000 ÷ 8 = 60 000 bytes.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A candidate's school entered the database elective and the web elective. On Paper 2 the candidate should:
options: A. Answer all three electives in full.
B. Skip Paper 1, because Paper 2 replaces it.
C. Invent a fourth elective on the day.
D. Answer the questions for those two electives, not a third elective the school did not enter.
questions.explanation: Paper 2 is the two options the school entered. Paper 1 is still the compulsory paper. Check the options on your entry, not a friend's.
questions.subject: ict

questions.question: A 2-mark question says "State the output" under a short algorithm. Which answer matches the command?
options: A. A paragraph that defines every keyword and never states the output.
B. The output value or text, after a trace, without a definition the question did not ask for.
C. A different algorithm you would have preferred to write.
D. An input the program never reads.
questions.explanation: State means give the result the trace produces. Extra definitions do not replace the missing output, and you must follow the algorithm that is printed.
